paper: Data Storage Without a Physical Location
kind: engineering structure (no claim); retrospective — predates the box kites
one_line: Every string already has a number (Horner bijection); store the index (address + length), traverse it by de Bruijn sequence, ledger each ingest as (index, timestamp), and fold the ledger's own index recursively — via the octonion — to a single 256-bit holographic root.
stored_artifacts: de Bruijn generator (k, n) + charset permutation
not_stored: per-item records beyond what the root unfolds to
bit_width_note: HyperWebster.md L6 states a 512-bit single-item address. The 256-bit figure here is the fixed-width root of the recursive index-of-index fold (this paper's D7), not the per-item address. Engine reports both.

hyper_indexer_lineage.category_definition: a hyper-indexer is a bijective unranking from an address into a structured object, where the address space is a 2^n-addressed hypercomplex basis, the enumeration is de-Bruijn-minimal, and the recursion is a Merkle-style fold to a fixed-width root; reconstruction is a pure function of the address and the fixed machinery
